title: Caesarea Maritima and the Pilate inscription
summary: At Caesarea Maritima, the Roman administrative seat of Judaea, Italian excavators found a limestone block in 1961 that had been reused as a theatre step. Its Latin dedication names Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judea and refers to a building for the emperor Tiberius. Dated to Pilate's term, 26–36 CE, the original is in the Israel Museum.

uncertainty.note: The inscription is dated only to the span of Pilate's prefecture (26–36 CE); the 1961 discovery is a separate event.

as_recorded.value: Pilate ruled Judaea during the period 26-36 AD

where.modern_name: Caesarea Maritima, Israel (find spot: the Roman theatre)

importance.justification: Contemporary stone evidence for the Roman prefect of the Gospel narratives, fixing his title as prefect and showing imperial-cult building at Caesarea.

reviewer_note: Dating rests on Pilate's term (26–36); no opened page gives a closer date for the dedication. Bible Odyssey says the 1961 Italian team found it in a late theatre rebuild; the Israel Museum location is from Saxum (the Israel Museum's own catalogue page could not be opened). The Tiberieum reading is partly conjectural and has been disputed.
